facts.subject: tomato
facts.value: Prune and safely destroy lower infected leaves touching the soil surface, maintain 60x45 cm plant spacing, and apply organic mulch to suppress rain splash inoculation of Alternaria spores.

evidence.source_title: Package of Practices for Commercial Tomato Cultivation in India
evidence.organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR)
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Sanitation through removal of bottom leaves and soil mulching with paddy straw reduces Alternaria inoculum pressure by up to 45%.

facts.subject: tomato
facts.value: Apply preventative foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum or Trichoderma viride @ 5-10 g/L or Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) during early vegetative stages.

evidence.source_title: Expert System for Crop Protection: Horticultural IPM Protocols
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Prophylactic application of Trichoderma viride formulation @ 10g/L significantly curtails early blight lesion development in field tomatoes.

facts.subject: tomato
facts.value: For moderate-to-severe established Early Blight infections, CIBRC approves Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L as contact protectants. Observe minimum 7-day pre-harvest interval (PHI) and rotate modes of action to prevent resistance.

evidence.source_title: Major Uses of Pesticides Registered Under the Insecticides Act, 1968
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Mancozeb 75% WP is officially labeled for Alternaria solani on Tomato at 1.5-2.0 kg/ha (2.0 g/L dilution) with a statutory waiting period of 7 days.

facts.subject: tomato
facts.value: Late blight (Phytophthora infestans) epidemics trigger rapidly when ambient temperatures remain between 18-22°C paired with continuous relative humidity > 90% or heavy overcast rainfall. Fields can face catastrophic defoliation within 48-72 hours.

evidence.source_title: Standard Operating Procedure for Weather-Based Crop Risk Warnings
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Foliar leaf wetness > 10 hours at temperatures 12-22°C represents critical high-risk threshold for late blight outbreak in Solanaceae.

facts.subject: tomato
facts.value: Eliminate overhead sprinkler irrigation completely; switch to drip or ground furrow watering. Bacterial spot spreads primarily through water droplets splashing between foliage.

evidence.source_title: Package of Practices for Commercial Tomato Cultivation in India
evidence.organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR)
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Avoiding overhead wetting prevents bacterial dispersal and reduces spot incidence by over 60%.

facts.subject: tomato
facts.value: Erect bright yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre) across field borders to intercept whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci). Immediately rogue out and burn stunted plants showing upward-cupped leaves within the first 30 days after transplanting.

conditions.symptom: stunting, upward leaf cupping, marginal yellowing

evidence.source_title: Package of Practices for Commercial Tomato Cultivation in India
evidence.organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR)
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Yellow sticky traps monitor whitefly build-up; early rogueing of viral foci prevents field-wide spread.

facts.subject: tomato
facts.value: Daytime temperatures consistently exceeding 35°C during flowering and fruit setting (35-65 DAS) cause flower abortion, pollen sterility, and poor fruit set. Provide light frequent furrow or drip irrigation to cool the root zone.

evidence.source_title: Package of Practices for Commercial Tomato Cultivation in India
evidence.organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR)
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Daytime temperatures consistently exceeding 35°C (especially during flowering and fruit setting stages, 35-65 DAS) cause severe flower abortion, pollen sterility, style elongation, and poor fruit set.

facts.subject: tomato
facts.value: Tomato foliage is sensitive to chilling injury when ambient night temperatures drop below 10°C, and ground frost (≤ 2°C) causes rapid foliar blackening and plant death. Use straw mulching or low agro-net tunnels for cold defense.

evidence.source_title: Package of Practices for Commercial Tomato Cultivation in India
evidence.organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR)
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Tomato foliage is highly tender and susceptible to chilling injury when ambient night temperatures drop below 10°C. Direct ground frost (temperatures ≤ 2°C) causes irreversible cellular freezing, leaf blackening, and plant death.

facts.subject: wheat
facts.value: Crown Root Initiation (CRI) stage, occurring 20 to 25 days after sowing, is the single most critical irrigation window for wheat in India. Moisture stress at CRI causes irreversible tillering reduction and up to 30-40% yield penalty.

evidence.source_title: Wheat Production Technology & Rust Resistance Management for Indo-Gangetic Plains
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: If only one irrigation is available, it must be applied at Crown Root Initiation (21-25 DAS) to secure root anchoring and tiller primordia.

facts.subject: wheat
facts.value: Terminal heat spikes exceeding 30-32°C during milking and grain filling stages (March-April) accelerate maturity and cause grain shrivelling. Light sprinkler or furrow irrigation during warm spells provides essential micro-climatic cooling.

evidence.source_title: Wheat Production Technology & Rust Resistance Management for Indo-Gangetic Plains
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: In Northern and Central India, sudden temperature spikes during the grain filling and milking stages (March-April) exceeding 30°C to 32°C accelerate crop maturity, curtail assimilate translocation, reduce thousand-grain weight, and cause shrivelled grains.

facts.subject: wheat
facts.value: Do not irrigate wheat fields when strong convective winds (>35-40 km/h) are forecast within 24-48 hours. Irrigating saturated soil under high winds induces severe stem and root lodging.

evidence.source_title: Wheat Production Technology & Rust Resistance Management for Indo-Gangetic Plains
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Never irrigate wheat fields when high winds or gusty rainstorms are forecast within 24-48 hours.

facts.subject: wheat
facts.value: Yellow / Stripe Rust (Puccinia striiformis) flourishes in cool, humid sub-mountainous and plains tracts when day temperatures range between 10-15°C with heavy morning fog or intermittent showers during December to February.

evidence.source_title: Wheat Production Technology & Rust Resistance Management for Indo-Gangetic Plains
evidence.section: Stripe Rust Epidemiology and Varietal Safeguards
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Continuous dew formation with daytime temperatures below 15°C accelerates yellow rust sporulation on susceptible varieties.

facts.subject: rice
facts.value: Avoid excessive nitrogen top-dressing. High nitrogen fertilizer application creates soft, succulent foliar tissues highly prone to Magnaporthe blast infection. Split nitrogen into 3-4 balanced doses paired with adequate potash.

evidence.source_title: Expert System for Crop Protection: Horticultural & Field Crop IPM Protocols
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Overuse of urea fertilizer without potash balance directly triggers virulent blast epidemics under cloudy Kharif conditions.

facts.subject: general
facts.value: After heavy unseasonal rains or severe waterlogging exceeding 24 hours, clear field drainage channels immediately to prevent root asphyxiation and soil-borne Phytophthora/Fusarium root rot. Do not apply heavy chemical sprays while soil is inundated.

evidence.source_title: Standard Operating Procedure for Weather-Based Crop Risk Warnings
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Excess surface stagnation must be drained within 12-24 hours to prevent anoxic root damage and secondary collar rot complexes.

facts.subject: general
facts.value: Agricultural Heatwave alert is triggered when maximum temperature reaches ≥ 40°C in plains (≥ 30°C in hills) or departure is ≥ 4.5°C from normal. High night temperatures (≥ 25°C) exacerbate crop respiration loss.

evidence.source_title: Standard Operating Procedure for Weather-Based Crop Risk Warnings
evidence.section: Heatwave & Dry Spell Criteria in Agriculture
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Agricultural Heatwave: Maximum temperature reaching ≥ 40°C in plains (or ≥ 30°C in hilly regions), or a departure of ≥ 4.5°C from normal maximum temperature sustained over 2 consecutive days.

facts.subject: general
facts.value: A dry spell is defined as 7 to 10 consecutive rainless days during active crop growth in rainfed tracts, creating acute root-zone moisture deficits and elevated reference evapotranspiration (ET0). Prioritize moisture conservation mulching.

evidence.source_title: Standard Operating Procedure for Weather-Based Crop Risk Warnings
evidence.section: Dry Spell Criteria in Rainfed Crops
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: A period of at least 7 to 10 consecutive rainless days during the active Kharif monsoon season in rainfed tracts, creating acute root-zone soil moisture deficits and accelerating reference evapotranspiration (ET0).
